content:
Following the release of the seventh developer betas for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and other upcoming Apple software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public betas. Here are the details.

Apple releases new public betas

Apple previously released:

  • iOS 27 developer beta 7 (build: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 developer beta 7 (build: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7 (build: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 developer beta 7 (build: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 developer beta 7 (build: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 developer beta 7 (build: 24R5358a)

Apple is now pushing the corresponding versions to public beta users, marking the fifth round of public beta releases. Apple has so far released new public betas for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's releases don't include any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now mainly focused on bug fixes and stability improvements ahead of the official launch in a few weeks.

Additionally, Apple earlier today released the second public release candidate (RC) of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), following the release of the corresponding developer release candidate. The second release candidate of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is also expected to be released soon. Available at 7:42 PM ET.

Across all releases today, the public beta build numbers match those of the corresponding developer betas.

Enroll in the Apple public beta program

To enroll your device in the public beta program, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each respective device. Here's how to install the public beta on iPhone:

  • Go to the Apple Beta Software Program website and select "Sign Up" or "Sign In."
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone, then accept the program terms and enroll your account.
  • Open Settings on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta."
  • Return to the Software Update page and tap "Update Now" when the beta appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you use your primary iPhone, make sure to back it up first.

Did you spot any changes in today's beta? Let us know in the comments.
